draftA: REQ-1 Flag a student when either condition holds: attendance below 90% over the last 20 school days, or two or more failing grades in the current term. Both signals are checked, and either one alone triggers the flag. Open point: the pass mark that defines a failing grade still needs confirming. REQ-2 Only the student's own counsellor and the head of year can see the flag. No other user can see it. REQ-3 The flag clears automatically only after neither condition has held for 10 consecutive school days. REQ-4 A new flag must reach the student's counsellor as soon as it is raised, so they can follow up within a week. AC-1 Attendance: a student present 17 of the last 20 school days (85%) with 0 failing grades is flagged. A student present 18 of 20 days (exactly 90%) is not flagged, because 90% is not below 90%. AC-2 Grades: a student with 20 of 20 days attended and 2 failing grades this term is flagged. With 1 failing grade this term they are not flagged. Failing grades from a previous term do not count. AC-3 Visibility: for a flagged student, their counsellor and the head of year can see the flag. A different student's counsellor and a subject teacher cannot. AC-4 Clearing: a flagged student who meets neither condition for 9 consecutive school days stays flagged, and the flag clears on day 10. If attendance falls below 90% on day 7, the student stays flagged and the 10-day count restarts once both conditions are clear again.
draftB:
REQ-1: Flag a student when attendance over the last 20 school days is below 90 percent, or when the student has two or more failing grades in the current term.
REQ-2: Show the flag only to the student's counsellor and the head of year, so the counsellor can follow up within a week.
REQ-3: Clear the flag when neither condition has held for 10 school days.
AC-1: A student with attendance below 90 percent over the last 20 school days, for example 89 percent, is flagged even with no failing grades.
AC-2: A student with two failing grades in the current term is flagged even if attendance over the last 20 school days is 90 percent; one failing grade with 90 percent attendance is not flagged.
AC-3: If neither condition holds for 10 school days, the flag clears; if attendance is still below 90 percent or failing grades are still two or more on day 10, the flag remains.
AC-4: The student's counsellor and the head of year can see the flag, and nobody else can.

reviewOfA.strengths: The draft correctly flags on either signal alone and keeps the worked figures exact, including 17 of 20 days at 85 percent flagged and exactly 90 percent not flagged.

findings.title: 89 percent example may be unachievable
findings.detail: If attendance is recorded per whole day, 20 days give 5-point steps: 17/20 is 85 percent and 18/20 is 90 percent, so 89 percent cannot occur. Testers may be unable to build this case. Use 17 of 20 days (85 percent), or state the recording unit.
findings.quote: for example 89 percent, is flagged even with no failing grades

findings.title: Clearing window reset not tested
findings.detail: AC-3 checks the conditions only on day 10. The facts require that neither condition has held for 10 school days. A case where a condition recurs mid-window, for example on day 5, and restarts the count should be specified and tested.
findings.quote: if attendance is still below 90 percent or failing grades are still two or more on day 10, the flag remains

reviewOfB.strengths: The requirements reproduce the requester's thresholds, visibility limits and clearing rule exactly, and AC-2 tests the 90 percent and one-failing-grade boundaries.

merge.keptFromA: I kept draft A's structure and exact worked figures (17 of 20 days at 85% flagged, 18 of 20 at exactly 90% not flagged), its pass-mark open point, its previous-term rule, its visibility test cases and its mid-window reset case.
merge.keptFromB: I kept draft B's boundary pairing in the grades test, where 90% attendance is combined with two failing grades (flagged) and with one failing grade (not flagged), and its check that the flag remains if a condition still holds on day 10.

resolutions.note: Replaced the 89 percent example with whole-day figures: 17 of 20 days (85%) is flagged and 18 of 20 days (90%) is not.

finalReview.strengths: The draft applies both stated triggers, limits visibility to the student's counsellor and the head of year, and uses the correct boundaries: 17 of 20 is 85 percent and flagged, exactly 90 percent is not below 90 percent, and the flag stays through nine clear days and clears on day 10.
